key_insight: TrajectoryFlowNet learns both how particles move and how the surrounding fluid flows from very limited trajectory measurements. Its physics-informed approach jointly predicts long-range particle paths and flow fields.
problem_solved: Reconstructing fluid motion from sparse particle observations is challenging, especially when both long-range trajectories and the underlying flow field must be inferred.
method: Connects a Lagrangian view of moving particles with an Eulerian view of flow across space.
Uses physics-informed learning to jointly predict particle trajectories and flow fields from limited trajectory measurements.
Validates the approach in simulations and blood-flow experiments.
impact: The work illustrates how physical constraints can support learning when observations are scarce. It offers a promising approach for AI-driven flow reconstruction and trajectory prediction, including blood-flow analysis.
visual_elements: Sparse observed particle tracks beside predicted long-range paths.
A paired diagram contrasting particle-following Lagrangian and spatial Eulerian views.
A workflow showing trajectory measurements entering TrajectoryFlowNet and producing paths plus a flow-field map.
Simulation and blood-flow experiment panels highlighting the two validation settings.
paper_title: Lagrangian–Eulerian learning of flow field and trajectories with TrajectoryFlowNet
paper_authors: Jingdi Wan, Hongping Wang, Bo Liu, Xiaolei Yang, Xiaodong Hu
